questions.question: A homologous series is a series of organic compounds that:
options: All have exactly the same molecular formula
Can be described by the same general formula, each member differing by a CH₂ unit

questions.question: A hydrocarbon is a compound that contains:
options: Carbon bonded to any other element

questions.question: A saturated organic compound is one that:
options: Contains at least one double bond
Is dissolved in water to its maximum amount

The functional group of the alcohols is:
options: The hydroxyl group, OH, bonded to a chain carbon

questions.question: Aldehydes and ketones both contain a carbonyl group. The difference is that in an aldehyde the carbonyl carbon:
options: Is bonded to two other carbons inside the chain
Carries an OH group as well
Is bonded to an oxygen chain
Sits at the end of the chain, bonded also to a hydrogen

questions.question: Which suffix belongs to the carboxylic acids?

The chain is numbered from the end that gives:
options: The alphabetically first substituent the lowest number
The functional group the lowest possible number
The most hydrogens to carbon one

Structural isomers are molecules with:
options: The same structural formula but different molecular formulae
The same molecular formula but different structural formulae
The same name but different formulae

questions.question: Butane and 2-methylpropane are examples of:
Butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol are positional isomers because they differ only in:
options: The length of the carbon chain
The homologous series they belong to
The position of the hydroxyl group on the same chain

questions.question: Propanal and propanone, both C₃H₆O, are:
options: Functional isomers — same formula, different homologous series

questions.question: In the name butan-2-ol, the part "but" tells you:
options: The OH group is on carbon 2
The main chain is four carbons long

questions.question: The suffix of an IUPAC name — like -anol or -anoic acid — works like a:
options: House number, locating the group on the chain
Family surname, telling you the functional group

questions.question: If counting from the left puts the OH at number 2 and from the right at number 3, the correct name uses:
options: Either number, since both describe the molecule
2, because the functional group takes the lowest number available

questions.question: In 1,2-dichloroethane, the "di" tells you:
options: The molecule has a double bond

questions.question: In any correct organic structure, every carbon atom must hold exactly:
options: As many bonds as there are hydrogens

questions.question: The recommended order for building a structure from a name is:
options: Hydrogens first, then the chain, then the branches
Carbon spine, then functional group and branches at their numbers, then hydrogens
Functional group first, then hydrogens, then the chain
Any order, as long as the atoms are all used

questions.question: In 2-methylbutane, the number of hydrogens on carbon 2 of the main chain is:
Finding a carbon with five bonds in your finished structure means:
options: The carbon carries a functional group
You have made an error — carbon can never bond five times

questions.question: Four carbons in a straight chain, and four carbons drawn with a bend in the middle of the drawing, are:
options: The same molecule — only the drawing bent, not the bonds

questions.question: To create a genuine chain isomer of pentane, you must:
options: Draw pentane vertically instead of horizontally
Add an extra carbon to the chain
Move a carbon off the end and bond it to a middle carbon, as in 2-methylbutane
